calls.headline: One-year bill yield hits 26.35%, highest since March 2024, as the dollar rises to 54.91
calls.body: The average yield on one-year treasury bills rose to 26.35% at Thursday's auction from 26.16% a week earlier, and the six-month yield to 25.74% from 25.36%; the central bank accepted EGP 87.2bn against a EGP 95bn target (Mubasher, Youlyou). Its dollar rate ended Thursday at EGP 54.77 buy and 54.91 sell, from 54.63 and 54.76. Futures price a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 as near certain, about 98% on CME's FedWatch (Gotrade, Coinpedia). The EGX30 fell 0.45% to 50,311.78 on EGP 6.58bn of turnover, but foreigners bought a net EGP 224.9m of shares while Egyptians sold 147.9m and Arabs 76.9m (Arab Finance, Masrawy).
calls.view: Egypt is paying more to keep foreign money as the Fed tightens, and taking less than it offered shows the central bank resisting a faster climb. That keeps the pound drifting, not breaking: the desk expects the dollar to stay below EGP 56.50 through December 17, with banks earning more on bills and developers paying more for credit. Foreign share buying on a down day is a small, steady vote for the market at these prices. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The central bank's dollar rate closes above EGP 56.50 before December 17, or the one-year yield jumps above 27% at the next auction.

calls.headline: Brent nears $98 after strikes on Kuwait and Jazan, before OPEC+ meets
calls.line: Dearer oil before a meeting expected to change nothing keeps Egypt's fuel bill high into December.
calls.body: Brent settled at $96.57 on Thursday, its highest since November 6, after drones hit a site in Kuwait and a projectile struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, and traded at $97.62–97.95 on Friday morning (AP, CNBC data via MLQ). It is heading for its first weekly gain in five weeks, though still down nearly 20% for November (Rigzone, citing Saxo Bank; MLQ). OPEC+ is expected to keep output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting, Reuters reported, after agreeing to hold them through December.
calls.view: With OPEC+ likely to stand pat, oil stays in a $90–100 range set by Gulf supply risk, at the dear end for Egypt, which imports fuel and LNG in dollars just as bill yields climb to hold foreign money. Refiners and petrochemical exporters gain on product prices; fuel users and the pound lose. Medium confidence on the range; low on the effect on stocks.
calls.wrong: OPEC+ agrees a larger 2027 increase than expected, or Brent closes below $90.

calls.headline: Suez transits run 31% above last November as container lines return
calls.line: Canal dollars are recovering faster than the Houthi threat to Saudi ports is growing, for now.
calls.body: In the week to November 22, 318 ships of 30.1m dwt crossed the canal, 31% more than the weekly average of November 2025 though 28% below pre-crisis tonnage, and container capacity reached 984,782 TEU, 24% below pre-crisis levels (Lloyd's List Intelligence). The Suez Canal Authority put revenue at $593m in the first weeks of November against $295m a year earlier, and Maersk told President Sisi it will restore its full network through the canal within months (DNE Africa).
calls.view: A second dollar source is rebuilding beside foreign bill buying, which softens the pound's exposure to a Fed hike. The risk is the Red Sea itself: the Houthis claimed attacks on Jeddah and Jazan this week. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: Weekly Suez transits fall back below the November 2025 average, or a major line suspends canal sailings again.

calls.headline: Orascom Construction rises 3.5% to EGP 790 as OCI leaves Amsterdam
calls.line: The rebound undoes Wednesday's fall, but 97.2m new shares reach OCI's holders around December 8.
calls.body: Orascom Construction rose 3.5% to EGP 790.00 on Thursday, OCI's last day of trading in Amsterdam before it delists on Friday. The combination added 97,201,359 shares, lifting the count to 207.4m from 110.2m; NNS Holding and the Sawiris family hold about 78% of OCI, and the new shares are credited on or around December 8 (EnterpriseAM, Prop News Time).
calls.view: About a fifth of the new shares go to holders outside the Sawiris family, some of whom bought OCI for its Dutch listing and may sell Egyptian shares; that supply can cap the stock into mid-December. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: The stock closes above EGP 830 before December 15.

calls.headline: AI credit scare: Oracle swaps hit a record, S&P puts Nvidia on watch
calls.body: Oracle opened 7.45% lower on Wednesday as its five-year credit-default swap spread hit a record, and closed down 5.1% at $103.88, about 10% below the $116 at which it sold 86.2m shares on November 2 (GuruFocus via TradingView, ABC News). S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia on CreditWatch negative, citing management and governance risks; Nvidia fell 3.9% to $149.30 and the Nasdaq dropped as much as 4.6% before closing 0.62% lower, while SoftBank's five-year swaps reached 501 bp, their widest since October 2022 (Reuters via Yahoo Finance and AOL). Nasdaq futures rose about 1% on Friday morning (TradingView).
calls.view: The credit market, not earnings, is now setting the price of AI spending: the companies that borrow to build data centers pay more each week, and Friday's thin rebound does not change that. The desk expects AI borrowers to lag the S&P 500 into the Fed's December 9 meeting. Low confidence: one strong guide or a calm Fed could reopen the bond market quickly.
calls.wrong: Oracle closes back above its $116 offer price, or its credit swaps narrow sharply, before December 31.

calls.headline: A December hike is priced at about 98%; the guidance is the risk
calls.line: With the hike already in prices, what the Fed signals for January moves stocks.
calls.body: CME's FedWatch puts the odds of a quarter-point rise at the December 8–9 meeting at about 98%, from a range of 3.75–4.00% (Gotrade, Coinpedia). The 10-year Treasury yield was 4.85% on Wednesday and rose toward 4.89% on Friday morning, with the dollar index near 103.8 (TradingView).
calls.view: The hike itself is no longer news; a statement that leaves January open would hit rate-sensitive stocks and help the dollar, while a signal of a pause would lift small caps and housing. The desk leans to the first, given hot growth. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: Futures odds for December fall below 70%, or the 10-year closes below 4.50%.

calls.headline: Brent heads for its first weekly gain in five weeks before OPEC+
calls.line: Gulf strikes keep a supply premium in oil, a support for energy stocks.
calls.body: Brent settled at $96.57 on Thursday, its highest since November 6, after strikes on Kuwait and Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, and traded near $98 on Friday morning; WTI was at about $86 (AP, CNBC data via MLQ). OPEC+ is expected to keep targets unchanged on Sunday (Reuters, via MLQ).
calls.view: A $90–100 range holds while Gulf attacks continue, which helps Exxon's cash flow and hurts airlines and consumers already paying more for credit. Low confidence for stocks: oil fell nearly 20% in November before this week.

calls.headline: HP jumps 11.5% on a revenue beat as memory costs squeeze its margins
calls.line: Memory now makes up 40% of a PC's bill of materials: good for chipmakers, hard on hardware makers.
calls.body: HP rose 11.5% to $31.15 on Wednesday, the S&P 500's biggest gain, after fourth-quarter revenue of $16.0bn beat the $15.3bn consensus; memory and storage now make up 40% of its PC bill of materials, and PC margins fell to 3.0% from 5.8% (TradingNEWS). Goldman Sachs, Barclays and BofA raised targets but kept sell ratings, and Bernstein called the beat low-quality because of tariff refunds (Yahoo Finance).
calls.view: The beat came from prices, not margins: hardware makers are passing on memory costs while their own margins shrink, so the rally rests on a quarter that analysts still rate a sell. Low confidence.
calls.wrong: HP holds above $31 through its next guidance update.

view.headline: The IMF and Suez hold the dollar below EGP 56.50
view.body: The pound slipped 0.3% to 54.91 on Thursday as one-year bills rose to 26.35%, but the IMF staff deal, a canal earning double last year's dollars and record remittances should keep the dollar below EGP 56.50 through the December 17 meeting. The risk is a Fed that hikes and signals more: bills would then need to climb further to hold foreign money.
